answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into a trust topology evaluated by game-theoretic multi-agent auditing. Graph verification isolates suspect nodes across a topological cut: a sparse cut acts like an impassable canyon partitioning collusive identities, while legitimate clusters flourish like an open meadow. When random auditing discovers Byzantine consensus, malicious stakes are slashed. Because verifying cut boundaries requires honest cross-links, faking valid connectivity induces superlinear attacker cost as the lotus network expands.
